column1: # Pull.fm - rule configuration for the PACKAGED ZAP scans (zap-baseline.py and
# zap-api-scan.py), which take this file with -c and the GitHub Action takes it
# as `rules_file_name`.
# TAB-SEPARATED. Format:  <ruleId>\t<IGNORE|WARN|FAIL>\t(<comment>)
# ZAP also accepts     :  <ruleId>\tOUTOFSCOPE\t<url regex>
# Do not convert the tabs to spaces; the parser is literal about them.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS ALONGSIDE security/zap/rules/alert-filters.yaml
# Two entrypoints, two config formats, same decisions:
#   - the Automation Framework plans under security/zap/plans/ are the primary
#     path and take their tuning from alert-filters.yaml;
#   - the packaged scans (a one-line docker run, and the zaproxy GitHub Action)
#     cannot read an AF plan and need this.
# Keep the two in agreement. Where they differ, alert-filters.yaml wins, because
# that is the file the gating scan actually reads.
# Grading intent, matching Gate 8 ("zero high/critical"):
#   FAIL   -> blocks the build
#   WARN   -> reported, does not block (run the packaged scan with -I)
#   IGNORE -> suppressed, and every IGNORE below must justify itself
# Rule ids and names verified against https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
# Transport and header controls. Gate 8 also requires Mozilla Observatory >= A+,
# which is broadly a restatement of these four passing.

column1: # Every line here is an assertion that the rule cannot produce a true positive
# against this system. If one of those assertions stops holding, the line is a
# vulnerability, so each carries its reason.

column3: (Timestamp Disclosure - Unix: every response is timestamped by design - wishlist created_at, connection access_expires_at, cursor payloads - so this fires on essentially every endpoint)

(Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments: matches SQL and debug keywords inside response bodies, and our bodies are artist names, album titles and biographies from MusicBrainz and Last.fm. There are no comments in JSON, so every hit is a keyword match on user-facing content)
(Permissions Policy Header Not Set: governs browser feature access on a document, and there is no document. The CSP above already denies everything)
(Dangerous JS Functions: requires JavaScript in the response, and this API serves none)
(Modern Web Application: informational, and always true of an API)

(HTTP Server Response Header: Cloudflare always answers "Server: cloudflare", which is neither hideable by us nor informative - the target's use of Cloudflare is visible from DNS. Note this is broader than the equivalent alert filter in alert-filters.yaml, which scopes the suppression by evidence so a leaked Fastify or Node version still alerts. The packaged-scan config format cannot express that, which is one reason the AF plan is the gating path)

column1: # 100000 and 100001 are raised only by zap-api-scan.py, which enables two extra
# passive scripts. Scoped rather than suppressed, because the 401/403/404
# responses this API returns to a foreign subject are the observable proof of the
# BOLA design (BOLA-TESTING.md) and must stay visible.
# /v1/artists/{mbid}/events returns 501 BY DESIGN: docs/PLAN.md §1 disables
# events because no provider was approved.

column3: .*/v1/artists/[^/]+/events.*

(Unexpected Content-Type was returned: fires on application/problem+json, which docs/PLAN.md §6 mandates for every error. Left as a warning so an unexpected text/html - which would mean requests are bypassing the app - still shows up)
